title: What Did the Work?
endLine: Life's chemistry follows ordinary rules, worked by catalysts we can isolate.

scenes.tts: Last time, juice pressed from yeast fermented sugar, and controls showed no living cell was needed. So if not life, what in that flask was doing the work?
scenes.narration: Last time, juice pressed from yeast fermented sugar, and controls showed no living cell was needed. So if not life, what in that flask was doing the work?
scenes.caption: Last time, juice pressed from yeast fermented sugar, and controls showed no living cell was needed. So if not life, what in that flask was doing the work?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's laboratory and colour map with no reset. COLOUR BY CONCEPT, as in the first film: GOLD specks = the vital force (now absent); TEAL = what was tested and found ordinary; the yeast cell is a large pale silhouette; sugar is a white block labelled SUGAR; carbon dioxide bubbles are white. New in this film: dissolved workers (enzymes) are rounded TEAL blobs with no internal structure; small helper tokens (cofactors) are PURPLE coins. Open on the first film's last picture: the broad platform labelled ORDINARY CHEMISTRY on the bench, holding a rock, a salt jar, the yeast cell silhouette and Buchner's flask of clear gold juice. The flask fills about 65% of the frame height at centre-right and bubbles steadily the whole film. On 'controls showed no living cell', a faint ghost of the first film's filter mesh and a CHLOROFORM drop flash at the flask neck, then fade for good. On the question, the camera pushes into the juice: a large dashed outline of an empty shape hovers in the liquid where something is clearly working, bubbles streaming off it. White text at top: WHAT DID THE WORK?
Title 'What Did the Work?' holds above the flask for 2 s while the top question text fades into it. The empty dashed outline keeps shedding bubbles inside the gold juice; the flask keeps bubbling.

scenes.tts: Buchner's answer lay in the juice itself. The carrier of the activity, he wrote, must be a dissolved substance, undoubtedly a protein. He named it zymase. His nineteen oh seven Nobel Prize is often called the first for a fundamentally biochemical discovery.
scenes.narration: Buchner's answer lay in the juice itself. The carrier of the activity, he wrote, must be a dissolved substance, undoubtedly a protein. He named it zymase. His 1907 Nobel Prize is often called the first for a fundamentally biochemical discovery.
scenes.caption: Buchner's answer lay in the juice itself. The carrier of the activity, he wrote, must be a dissolved substance, undoubtedly a protein. He named it zymase. His 1907 Nobel Prize is often called the first for a fundamentally biochemical discovery.
scenes.visual: Stay inside the juice. On 'dissolved substance', the dashed outline fills in as one large rounded TEAL blob, no internal structure, drifting in the liquid. A SUGAR block drifts into it and white bubbles leave it. On 'He named it zymase', a label ZYMASE attaches to the blob. On 'Nobel Prize', a small medal with '1907' settles on the flask's label at the edge of the frame; the blob keeps working the whole time.

scenes.tts: His worker had relatives. Some ferments, such as pepsin and the invertase of yeast, already worked outside cells. In eighteen seventy-seven, Wilhelm Kuehne named them enzymes, from the Greek for in leaven.
scenes.narration: His worker had relatives. Some ferments, such as pepsin and the invertase of yeast, already worked outside cells. In 1877, Wilhelm Kühne named them enzymes, from the Greek for "in leaven".
scenes.caption: His worker had relatives. Some ferments, such as pepsin and the invertase of yeast, already worked outside cells. In 1877, Wilhelm Kühne named them enzymes, from the Greek for "in leaven".
scenes.visual: Pull back out of the flask to the bench. Beside Buchner's flask, two small open dishes slide in on the platform, each holding a smaller TEAL blob at work on a white block: one labelled PEPSIN, one labelled INVERTASE. No cell silhouette surrounds either. On '1877', a brass plate labelled ENZYME, 'IN LEAVEN' slides under the two dishes and the ZYMASE flask together, joining all three as one family. The flask keeps bubbling; the dish blobs keep chipping at their blocks.

scenes.tts: Kuehne studied digestion and vision, and believed both were chemistry waiting to be lifted out of the cell. His word named the chemical worker, not the cell or the tissue.
scenes.narration: Kühne studied digestion and vision, and believed both were chemistry waiting to be lifted out of the cell. His word named the chemical worker, not the cell or the tissue.
scenes.caption: Kühne studied digestion and vision, and believed both were chemistry waiting to be lifted out of the cell. His word named the chemical worker, not the cell or the tissue.
scenes.visual: On 'digestion and vision', two simple outline icons appear beside the dishes, a STOMACH and an EYE, each with a TEAL blob glowing inside it. On 'lifted out of the cell', each blob rises out of its icon on a short arrow into its own small unlabelled dish. On 'not the cell or the tissue', the large yeast silhouette and the two icons dim while the TEAL blobs in the dishes and the zymase flask brighten together under the ENZYME plate.

scenes.tts: Workers are half the story. The other half is the rules. In eighteen fifty-four, Marcellin Berthelot joined glycerol to fatty acids and remade natural fats, releasing water. Add water, and the reaction runs back.
scenes.narration: Workers are half the story. The other half is the rules. In 1854, Marcellin Berthelot joined glycerol to fatty acids and remade natural fats, releasing water. Add water, and the reaction runs back.
scenes.caption: Workers are half the story. The other half is the rules. In 1854, Marcellin Berthelot joined glycerol to fatty acids and remade natural fats, releasing water. Add water, and the reaction runs back.
scenes.visual: The dishes slide to the back of the platform; Buchner's flask stays at left, still bubbling. At centre, a large white block labelled GLYCEROL with three sockets; three long strips labelled FATTY ACID click into the sockets one by one, and as each clicks a blue water drop falls out, three drops in all. The joined shape relabels FAT. On 'Add water', the three drops rise back, the strips unclip, and the pieces separate again. The join and split then repeat slowly in the background for the rest of the scene. Draw no atoms or bonds.

scenes.tts: That back-and-forth is equilibrium chemistry, the same kind that governs reactions in the mineral world. The body's molecules needed no special law. Berthelot also made new fats that nature does not.
scenes.narration: That back-and-forth is equilibrium chemistry, the same kind that governs reactions in the mineral world. The body's molecules needed no special law. Berthelot also made new fats that nature does not.
scenes.caption: That back-and-forth is equilibrium chemistry, the same kind that governs reactions in the mineral world. The body's molecules needed no special law. Berthelot also made new fats that nature does not.
scenes.visual: A large two-way arrow labelled EQUILIBRIUM appears under the joining and splitting fat. On 'mineral world', the rock and salt jar on the platform get an identical two-way arrow, pulsing in step with the fat's arrow. On 'no special law', a faint GOLD speck tries to settle on the fat and drifts away unused. On 'new fats', one strip is swapped for a differently coloured strip and the shape relabels NEW FAT, still joining and splitting.

scenes.tts: So here is the one idea. Where vitalists placed a force, chemists found ordinary chemistry. Its catalysts can be lifted out of the cell. And they follow the same rules as everything else.
scenes.narration: So here is the one idea. Where vitalists placed a force, chemists found ordinary chemistry. Its catalysts can be lifted out of the cell. And they follow the same rules as everything else.
scenes.caption: So here is the one idea. Where vitalists placed a force, chemists found ordinary chemistry. Its catalysts can be lifted out of the cell. And they follow the same rules as everything else.
scenes.visual: Bring the two halves together on the platform: at left the TEAL workers (zymase flask and the two dishes under the ENZYME plate), at right the joining-and-splitting fat with its EQUILIBRIUM arrow, beside the rock and salt jar. On 'Its catalysts can be lifted out', the TEAL zymase blob lifts out of a ghost yeast silhouette into the flask. On 'same rules', a TEAL band labelled SAME RULES runs under everything on the platform. Large white line at top: CATALYSTS + ORDINARY RULES.

scenes.tts: Buchner gave his worker one name. Predict: when chemists later took zymase apart, did they find a single substance, or several?
scenes.narration: Buchner gave his worker one name. Predict: when chemists later took zymase apart, did they find a single substance, or several?
scenes.caption: Buchner gave his worker one name. Predict: when chemists later took zymase apart, did they find a single substance, or several?
scenes.visual: Push back into Buchner's flask. The single large TEAL ZYMASE blob fills about 60% of the frame height, slowly turning, sugar going in and bubbles coming out. Question card at top in white: ONE OR SEVERAL? Do not split the blob or hint at an answer.
Predict pause. The question card ONE OR SEVERAL? stays. The ZYMASE blob turns slowly; sugar keeps drifting in and bubbles keep rising. Nothing else changes.

scenes.tts: Several. Harden and Young split zymase into enzymes plus small, heat-stable cofactors. Chief among them was cozymase, now known as N A D. Together they run glycolysis, plus two steps that make ethanol. A whole process had become a set of reactions, open to study one at a time.
scenes.narration: Several. Harden and Young split zymase into enzymes plus small, heat-stable cofactors. Chief among them was cozymase, now known as NAD. Together they run glycolysis, plus two steps that make ethanol. A whole process had become a set of reactions, open to study one at a time.
scenes.caption: Several. Harden and Young split zymase into enzymes plus small, heat-stable cofactors. Chief among them was cozymase, now known as NAD. Together they run glycolysis, plus two steps that make ethanol. A whole process had become a set of reactions, open to study one at a time.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves. On 'split zymase', the big TEAL blob separates into a horizontal chain of smaller TEAL blobs, labelled ENZYMES, plus a few small PURPLE coins labelled COFACTORS; tag the chain SCHEMATIC (the number of blobs is not a claim). On 'cozymase', one PURPLE coin enlarges and its label reads COZYMASE, then changes to NAD; the coins keep hopping between neighbouring blobs. On 'glycolysis', a SUGAR block enters the left end and is passed blob to blob; a bracket over most of the chain reads GLYCOLYSIS and a short bracket over the last two blobs reads 2 STEPS. An ETHANOL block leaves the right end with white bubbles. On 'one at a time', a spotlight isolates a single blob and its block, then widens again.

scenes.tts: The catalysts Kuehne named and Buchner freed are, nearly all of them, proteins. Even Woehler's urea, made in a flask with no kidney, has its own team. Your liver builds it right now with five enzymes, working in a loop called the urea cycle.
scenes.narration: The catalysts Kühne named and Buchner freed are, nearly all of them, proteins. Even Wöhler's urea, made in a flask with no kidney, has its own team. Your liver builds it right now with five enzymes, working in a loop called the urea cycle.
scenes.caption: The catalysts Kühne named and Buchner freed are, nearly all of them, proteins. Even Wöhler's urea, made in a flask with no kidney, has its own team. Your liver builds it right now with five enzymes, working in a loop called the urea cycle.
scenes.visual: On 'nearly all of them, proteins', every TEAL blob on screen gets a small tag PROTEIN; the PURPLE coins stay untagged. Pull back to the bench; the enzyme chain shrinks into Buchner's flask. On 'Woehler's urea', a block labelled UREA appears beside a small flask, a callback to the first film. On 'your liver', a large simple liver silhouette fills the right of the frame; inside it five TEAL blobs sit around a circular track labelled UREA CYCLE, passing a white block around the loop until a UREA block drops out. Label: 5 ENZYMES. The loop keeps turning.

scenes.tts: In the chemistry of the cell, the vital force had nowhere left to hide. In its place: workers you can pull out and study, obeying the same rules that govern rocks and salts.
scenes.narration: In the chemistry of the cell, the vital force had nowhere left to hide. In its place: workers you can pull out and study, obeying the same rules that govern rocks and salts.
scenes.caption: In the chemistry of the cell, the vital force had nowhere left to hide. In its place: workers you can pull out and study, obeying the same rules that govern rocks and salts.
scenes.visual: Return to the full platform labelled ORDINARY CHEMISTRY: Buchner's bubbling flask, the turning urea loop in the liver, the joining-and-splitting fat, the rock and salt jar. On 'nowhere left to hide', the last few GOLD specks drift up and fade out of the frame. On 'pull out and study', one TEAL blob lifts from the liver loop into a small separate dish and keeps working there. On 'rocks and salts', the TEAL SAME RULES band glows under every object.

End card over the dimmed but still moving laboratory: Buchner's flask keeps bubbling, TEAL workers keep turning in the urea loop. Large centred white text: 'Life's chemistry follows ordinary rules, worked by catalysts we can isolate.' Hex stands beside it and waves. Keep the line on screen through the final frame.
